title: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work-Until They Don't
abstract: arXiv:2608.14036v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Skills have emerged as a practical and effective approach for enhancing LLM agents at inference time through structured packages of knowledge. However, existing evaluations largely measure whether skills improve aggregated task success, leaving a more fundamental question underexplored: \emph{\textbf{When do skills help, why do they work, and where do they fail?}} Through controlled experiments across various benchmarks, agent harnesses and LLMs, we isolate the effects of representation, outcome annotation, retrieval difficulty, and cross-framework robustness of skills. translated_title: 揭秘智能体技能：为何它们有效——直至失效
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.14036v1 公告类型：新 摘要：技能已成为一种实用且有效的方法，通过在推理时提供结构化知识包来增强LLM智能体。然而，现有评估主要衡量技能是否提升聚合任务成功率，留下了一个更根本的问题未被充分探索：\emph{\textbf{技能何时有帮助，为何有效，以及在哪里失效？}}通过在多种基准、智能体框架和LLM上进行受控实验，我们隔离了表示、结果标注、检索难度以及技能的跨框架鲁棒性等因素的影响。为进一步回答这一问题，我们设计了一项对比研究，将受控定量实验与配对轨迹分析相结合。我们标准化了来自受控实验的8,135条试验记录，并从240条开放编码记录中保留了238个有效的唯一标签。我们将这些观察结果整合为一个包含三个高层面类别和十二种技能使用模式的分类体系。
tldr: 本文通过受控实验和轨迹分析，系统揭示了LLM智能体技能在何种条件下有效、为何有效及其失效原因，并构建了包含三类十二种模式的技能使用分类体系。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically reveals when, why, and how LLM agent skills work or fail through controlled experiments and trajectory analysis, establishing a taxonomy of three categories and twelve skill-use patterns.
